issues.legal_issue: A landlord may apply for fixation of fair rent while a contractual tenancy remains in force.
material_facts: The tenants occupied the building under a registered lease that had not expired when the landlords applied for fixation of fair rent.
The landlords acquired the building and applied under the rent-control legislation during the continuing tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The landlord may apply for fixation of fair rent during the subsistence of a contractual tenancy, and the fair rent fixed is payable during the contract period as well as afterwards.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(6), 2(8), 4, 5 and 7 of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, read as a whole, establish a scheme covering contractual and statutory tenancies; fair rent is fixed for the building and may be sought by either landlord or tenant. The Court held that general observations in Bhaiya Punjalal Bhagwanddin v. Dave Bhagwat Prabhuprasad and Manujendra v. Purendu Prasad were obiter and should not be applied without examining the scheme of the particular enactment. It distinguished the statutory schemes considered in those cases and referred to Rai Brij Raj Krishna v. S.K. Shaw and Bros., Hem Chand v. Sham Devi, R. Krishnamurthy v. Parthasarathy, Abbasbhai’s case and Mangilal v. Sugarchand Rathi.

predicates.rent_control_fair_rent_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an application to fix fair rent under rent-control legislation.
predicates.landlord_seeks_fair_rent: The landlord applied to have fair rent fixed for the building.
predicates.statutory_scheme_covers_contractual_tena: The applicable statutory scheme provides for fair-rent fixation in relation to contractual as well as statutory tenancies.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks fair rent in a proceeding under a scheme that covers contractual tenancies, the landlord may apply before the contractual tenancy ends.

issues.legal_issue: A variation of rent reserved by a registered lease must be made by another registered instrument and cannot be proved through evidence barred by the rule against varying a written contract.
material_facts: The rent was reserved by a registered lease deed.
The parties later allegedly agreed to increase the rent, but that variation was not made by another registered instrument.
The correspondence showed that the later agreement concerned payment of increased rent.
issues.conclusion: The evidence of the later agreement varying the rent was barred, and the variation could not be relied on.
issues.legal_principle: Section 92 of the Evidence Act bars evidence of an agreement or statement offered to contradict, vary, add to or subtract from the terms of a written contract, subject to its stated exceptions. A variation of rent reserved by a registered lease deed must be made by another registered instrument.

rule.if: rent_control_fair_rent_proceeding and registered_lease_reserves_rent and later_agreement_changes_reserved_rent and no_registered_variation

predicates.rent_control_fair_rent_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the rent payable for a building in a rent-control matter.
predicates.registered_lease_reserves_rent: The parties reserved the rent in a registered lease.
predicates.later_agreement_changes_reserved_rent: The parties later allegedly agreed to change the rent reserved in the lease.
predicates.no_registered_variation: The alleged change was not recorded in another registered instrument.

issues.definition: When a later agreement changes rent reserved in a registered lease without another registered instrument, that change cannot be proved in the proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A building is not excluded from rent-control legislation by a rent threshold when the valid rent, after disregarding an inadmissible variation, is below the applicable threshold.
material_facts: The rent reserved by the registered lease, without the alleged inadmissible increase, was below the applicable monthly exclusion threshold.
The asserted increase depended on an unregistered variation that could not be proved.
The landlords sought fixation of fair rent and the tenants challenged the Rent Controller’s jurisdiction on the basis of the higher asserted rent.
issues.conclusion: The building was not outside the Act on the basis of the asserted higher rent, and the Rent Controller had jurisdiction to entertain the fair-rent application.
issues.legal_principle: The applicable exclusion from the Act depended on the rent payable for the building. Because section 92 of the Evidence Act barred proof of the alleged variation to the registered lease, the rent reserved by that lease was the relevant rent for deciding whether the exclusion applied.

predicates.rent_control_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether a building is subject to rent-control legislation and whether fair rent may be fixed for it.
predicates.valid_rent_below_applicable_exclusion_th: The rent established by admissible evidence is below the threshold that would exclude the building from the legislation.

issues.definition: If admissible evidence establishes rent below the applicable exclusion threshold in a rent-control proceeding, the Rent Controller has jurisdiction.
